_doc: Every AI model routing registry in this repository. cloud-keyboard and cloud-mail each bake their OWN copy of the model table into their own BuildConfig, and that is deliberate — mail's text-tool settings are free to diverge from the keyboard's. What is NOT free to diverge is the truth: every copy prices the same OpenRouter models, so every copy has to be cross-checked against the live catalogue. The live blocks of test-keyboard-ai-routing.sh iterate THIS list, so a third app that copies the table is covered the moment it is listed here — and until it is listed, nothing anywhere checks it. That is exactly how one copy stayed unexamined while the other was tested.
_doc_fields: path: repo-relative build.json holding the registry. key: its top-level object in that file. label: the name a failure line prints, so a drift says WHICH app is stale rather than just which model. sources: the directories that application's own build and code live in, used by test-keyboard-text-resume.sh to prove no application resolves ANOTHER application's key — that check used to name the two keys and the two directory sets in the script, so a third application was not merely unchecked, it was invisible to the check that exists to catch exactly this.
_doc_ci: 1_cicd/src/cicd/test-ai-model-registry.yml runs those blocks on a schedule as well as on push. The schedule is the point: a baked price goes stale because the provider changed its mind, which produces no commit, so a push-triggered check alone can never see it.

registries._doc: cloud-writer, the application the owner asked for. It ROUTES like cloud-mail and holds no key, but it carries the same OpenRouter model table, so the same live cross-check has to reach it — and per the note above, until it appeared here nothing anywhere checked it. It is also the first registry with a MODEL PER TOOL; the tool choice is a preference in the application, not a field here, so nothing in this file changes shape for it.
